Observation Log:

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/03/17 (Fri) 13:15
[USER] User is using macOS.
[USER] User wants to remove all subfolders which have names ending with the character "2".
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant suggested using the command line tool "rm" to remove subfolders.
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided an example command: `find . -type d -name "*2" -exec rm -rf {} +`.
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The `find` command looks for directories (`-type d`) with a name that matches the pattern `*2`.
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The `-exec` flag runs the `rm -rf` command on each directory that matches the pattern.
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The `+` at the end of the `-exec` flag allows `find` to pass multiple arguments to `rm`.
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant cautioned the user to be careful when using the command, as it will delete the folder and all of the files and subfolders within it.
